name: The Rex Hotel Jazz & Blues Bar
Baro
sunNotes: 4th floor glassed-in and enclosed rooftop patio. Heated and covered year-round. The glass enclosure means no direct sun exposure for sun-tracking purposes even though it is a rooftop. Surrounded by taller King West condo towers.

name: Harriet's Rooftop
sunNotes: 16th floor rooftop at 1 Hotel Toronto (~56m). Open-air terrace with retractable glass roof (can be open in good weather). High enough to clear most King West mid-rises. Some taller condo towers nearby may shade briefly in early morning or late evening. Excellent sun exposure most of the day. Pool area adjacent.

name: C'est What
sunNotes: Beer garden is in a parking lot east of the building, accessed off The Esplanade. Canopies cover some seating. Financial district towers to the west cast long afternoon shadows. Gets morning and early afternoon sun from the east/south. Loses sun by mid-afternoon as tall buildings to the west shade the area.

name: Bar Raval
sunNotes: Tiny heated sidewalk patio on the south side of College St. Covered/sheltered seating means no direct sun reaches the patio regardless of time of day. A shaded spot by design.

name: Birreria Volo
sunNotes: Backyard patio behind a 2-storey building on the south side of College St. Cedar-walled laneway leads to picnic tables at rear. Building shades patio in afternoon as sun moves west. Best sun midday when sun is high enough to clear the roofline. Loses sun by mid-afternoon.

name: The Horseshoe Tavern
sunNotes: Small sidewalk patio on the south side of Queen St W at the northeast corner of Queen and Spadina. Historic 2-storey building (built 1861) is behind (north). South-facing so gets midday sun. Buildings across Queen are low-rise. Gets decent afternoon sun until late afternoon when western buildings start shading.

name: Bar Isabel
sunNotes: CafeTO sidewalk patio on the south side of College St. 2-storey building is behind (north) so it does not block sun. South-facing with low-rise buildings across the street. Gets good midday and afternoon sun until buildings to the west start shading it.

name: The Cameron House
sunNotes: Tiny sidewalk cafe patio on south side of Queen St W. 2-storey building with famous psychedelic mural is behind (north). South-facing with low-rise buildings across the street. Gets midday through early afternoon sun. Very small patio so even partial shadow covers the whole space.

name: Get Well
sunNotes: Patio on the north side of Dundas St W (south side of the building). Dundas runs roughly east-west here. The bar's own building is to the south, and the patio faces north toward the street. Gets limited sun when the sun is high enough to clear rooflines. Best midday sun in summer only. Patio lanterns suggest it is used more for evening ambiance.

name: The Fifth Social Club
sunNotes: Rooftop terrace atop the 5-storey heritage Gelber warehouse. At ~18m the patio clears most immediate neighbours but taller entertainment district towers to the east and west will shade it in early morning and late afternoon. Good midday and afternoon sun. Open-air section gets direct sun most of the day.

name: Kost
sunNotes: 44th floor rooftop at the Bisha Hotel, ~154m elevation. At this height, virtually nothing blocks the sun. Panoramic 360-degree views of the city and Lake Ontario. Only the CN Tower spire is taller nearby but it is too thin to cast meaningful shadow. Gets sun from sunrise to sunset, all day long. The best sun exposure of any patio in Toronto.

name: Terroni on Adelaide
sunNotes: Secret garden courtyard patio behind the 1852 York County Courthouse heritage building (3 storeys). Courtyard is somewhat enclosed by the building itself and neighbouring structures. Financial district towers are several blocks away but cast long shadows. Gets midday sun when the sun is high and to the south, but loses it by mid-afternoon. Charming but limited sun window.

name: Cibo Wine Bar
sunNotes: NOTE: No confirmed Cibo Wine Bar at 1055 Yonge. Yonge St location was at 2472 Yonge (now closed). Active Cibo locations are 522 King St W and 133 Yorkville Ave. If this address is correct, patio would be west-facing on Yonge. Gets afternoon and evening sun as sun moves west. Own building to the east blocks morning sun. Good late-afternoon sun in summer.

name: Pauper's Pub
sunNotes: 3rd floor rooftop patio atop a century-old building (former CIBC bank branch). At ~10.5m the rooftop is above the surrounding Annex low-rise buildings. High fences provide privacy but do not significantly block sun. Excellent sun exposure from late morning through evening. The Annex neighbourhood is mostly 2-3 storey houses so very few shadows. Also has a sidewalk patio at ground level.

name: Sweaty Betty's
sunNotes: Rear backyard patio behind the bar, covered with a pergola-style roof. The covered/sheltered design means no direct sun reaches patrons. Heated for cooler weather. A cozy shaded retreat by design, not a sun-seeking destination.

name: Pennylick
sunNotes: NOTE: Could not verify this venue exists at this address. Augusta Ave runs roughly north-south in Kensington Market. If on the west side of Augusta, patio faces west with the building to the east. Would get afternoon and evening sun. Kensington is low-rise (2-3 storeys) so few tall shadows. Assuming a typical Kensington sidewalk setup.

name: Bar Eugenie (formerly The Harbord Room)
sunNotes: NOTE: The Harbord Room is permanently closed. Now Bar Eugenie (opened Sept 2025). Backyard patio behind the building (north side). ~30-40 seats outdoors. Building is to the south, shading the patio for much of the day. Gets sun when it is high enough to clear the 3-storey roofline (midday in summer). Harbord Village is low-rise residential so no tall towers. Loses sun by mid-afternoon as building casts shadow northward.

name: The Emmet Ray
sunNotes: Small 16-seat sidewalk patio on the south side of College St. 2-storey building behind (north). South-facing with low-rise buildings across the street. Gets midday through mid-afternoon sun. College St runs E-W here; buildings to west shade in late afternoon.

name: Eastbound Brewing Co.
sunNotes: Streetside sidewalk patio on south side of Queen St E. Single-storey brewery behind (north). South-facing in low-rise Riverside. Wide Queen St and low buildings across the street. Excellent midday through late afternoon sun.

name: Left Field Brewery
sunNotes: Industrial warehouse brewery on short dead-end street. Outdoor picnic tables in parking area south/front of building. Low-rise industrial surroundings with no tall structures. Excellent sun from late morning through sunset. One of the sunniest brewery patios in the east end.

name: Bandit Brewery
sunNotes: Large tree-lined sidewalk patio on south side of Dundas St W with picnic tables and string lights. Also has heated glass-enclosed section (no direct sun there). Open patio is south-facing in low-rise area. Midday through mid-afternoon sun. Trees provide dappled shade in summer.

name: Blood Brothers Brewing
sunNotes: 50-seat patio in front of renovated century-old horse stable on south side of Geary Ave. Low-rise industrial strip running E-W. Single-storey buildings across street, no tall buildings nearby. Excellent sun from mid-morning through late afternoon.

name: Henderson Brewing
sunNotes: Courtyard patio on east side of brewery in Sterling Rd arts/industrial cluster. Surrounded by converted industrial buildings of similar height. East-facing means good morning sun but brewery building blocks afternoon sun from west. Best sun mid-morning to early afternoon.

name: Radical Road Brewing
sunNotes: Small sidewalk and curb lane patio on south side of Queen St E with astro-turf and vine-covered fence. Single-storey storefront. South-facing in low-rise Leslieville. Midday through mid-afternoon sun. Small enough that even slight shadows cover entire space.

name: Aloette Spadina
sunNotes: Streetside patio on west side of Spadina Ave (Alo restaurant is on 3rd floor above). Spadina is a wide N-S avenue. West-facing so no morning sun; building is to east. Gets afternoon and evening sun. Best from 1pm onward in summer. Wide Spadina means less shading from across the street.

name: Beso by Patria
sunNotes: Screened-in courtyard patio behind building (north side) with exposed brick and white globe lanterns. Enclosed on multiple sides by 2-3 storey buildings. Limited direct sun. Gets overhead sun midday in summer only. Mostly shaded, atmospheric patio.

name: Miss Thing's
sunNotes: Small sidewalk patio on south side of Queen St W in Parkdale. 2-storey commercial building behind (north). South-facing in low-rise stretch. Midday through mid-afternoon sun. Some shade from awnings and neighbouring buildings late afternoon.

name: Reposado Bar & Bodega
sunNotes: Covered back garden patio behind bar (north side). Dark stained wood and green plants. Covered/heated structure means very limited direct sun. Surrounding 2-3 storey Ossington buildings further block sun. Only midday overhead sun in summer reaches uncovered sections. A deliberately shaded, moody space.

name: Supermarket
sunNotes: Sidewalk patio on Augusta Ave facing east, south of College St in Kensington Market. Augusta runs N-S. Iron gate separates from pedestrians. String lights and greenery. East-facing gets morning and midday sun. Buildings across narrow Augusta block afternoon western sun. Best sun before 2pm.

name: Northern Belle
sunNotes: Street-level sidewalk patio on south side of Dundas St W, one block from Trinity Bellwoods Park. 2-storey building behind (north). South-facing with low-rise neighbourhood. Midday through mid-afternoon sun. Prime Dundas West people-watching patio.

name: The Dock Ellis
sunNotes: Small sidewalk patio on south side of Dundas St W at Dovercourt. 2-storey building behind (north). South-facing on low-rise stretch. Midday through mid-afternoon sun. Same owner as Emmet Ray, similar small-bar sidewalk setup.

name: Betty's East
sunNotes: Spacious sidewalk patio with large orange umbrellas and picnic tables on south side of Queen St E outside CoMMO building in Leslieville. South-facing in low-rise stretch. Wide Queen St and low buildings across street mean excellent sun. Late morning through late afternoon sun. One of Leslieville's sunniest patios.

name: Chamberlain's Pony Bar
sunNotes: Front patio faces north onto King St, partially covered by awnings. Side patio on Portland St faces west - gets strong afternoon sun from 2pm onward.
